edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults with severe or treatment-resistant depression
edges.mechanism: ECT likely works through broad neuroplastic and network-reset effects; clinically, it remains one of the fastest ways to reverse severe treatment-resistant depression.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2026 Traynor meta analysis in Am J Psychiatry, which ties electroconvulsive therapy to depression in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
